board_events.text: Resonances at 250, 350, 450 Hz; speed of sound 340 m/s. Find pipe type, fundamental, and length.
Successive gap is constant: 350 minus 250 = 100, and 450 minus 350 = 100.
Test open: if f1 = 100, then 250 over 100 = 2.5, not an integer. So it cannot be open - it is closed.
Answer: closed pipe, fundamental 50 Hz, length 1.7 m.

segments.text: A satisfying J E E Main puzzle. A pipe shows three successive resonances at two hundred fifty, three hundred fifty, and four hundred fifty hertz, with the speed of sound three hundred forty metres per second. Find whether the pipe is open or closed, its fundamental, and its length.
Start by reading the spacing off the spectrum. The gaps between successive resonances are both exactly one hundred hertz.
So the whole problem hinges on interpreting that constant gap of one hundred.
That gap equals the fundamental for an open pipe, but twice the fundamental for a closed pipe. Those are the only two options, and one simple test decides.

Test open. If the fundamental were one hundred, then two hundred fifty divided by one hundred is two point five, which is not a whole number, so two hundred fifty could not be a harmonic of a one hundred hertz open pipe. Open is ruled out, so it must be closed.

<excited>For a closed pipe the gap between successive odd harmonics is twice the fundamental, so two f one equals one hundred, giving a fundamental of fifty hertz. Check it: two hundred fifty, three hundred fifty, four hundred fifty are the fifth, seventh, and ninth harmonics, all odd.</excited>
Finally the length. For a closed pipe the fundamental is v over four L, so L is v over four f one, that is three hundred forty over two hundred, which is one point seven metres.
So the full answer: a closed pipe, fundamental fifty hertz, length one point seven metres.

एक satisfying J E E Main puzzle। एक pipe तीन successive resonances दिखाता है two hundred fifty, three hundred fifty, और four hundred fifty hertz पर, speed of sound three hundred forty metre per second। पता करो pipe open है या closed, उसका fundamental, और length।
Spectrum से spacing पढ़कर शुरू करो। Successive resonances के बीच के gaps दोनों बिल्कुल one hundred hertz हैं।
तो पूरी problem उस constant gap one hundred को interpret करने पर टिकी है।
वो gap open pipe के लिए fundamental के बराबर है, पर closed pipe के लिए fundamental का दोगुना। यही दो options हैं, और एक simple test decide कर देता है।

<whisper>Open test करो। अगर fundamental one hundred होता, तो two hundred fifty divided by one hundred है two point five, जो whole number नहीं, तो two hundred fifty किसी one hundred hertz open pipe का harmonic हो ही नहीं सकता। Open रद्द, तो closed होना चाहिए।</whisper>

Closed pipe के लिए successive odd harmonics के बीच gap fundamental का दोगुना है, तो two f one equals one hundred, fundamental fifty hertz। Check करो — two hundred fifty, three hundred fifty, four hundred fifty हैं fifth, seventh, ninth harmonics, सब odd।
आख़िर में length। Closed pipe के लिए fundamental है v over four L, तो L है v over four f one, यानी three hundred forty over two hundred, जो one point seven metre।
तो पूरा answer — closed pipe, fundamental fifty hertz, length one point seven metre।

First resonance at a quarter wave, second at three-quarter wave, both measured from the antinode above the rim.
Subtracting the two resonance conditions kills the end correction - that is the master move.

segments.text: The J E E Advanced version, where the end correction finally matters. A tuning fork of four hundred eighty hertz drives a resonance tube. The first resonance appears when the air column is seventeen centimetres, the second at fifty two centimetres. Find the speed of sound and the end correction.

The insight is in the figure. A resonance tube is a closed pipe, because the water surface acts as the sealed closed end. The first resonance is a quarter wave, the second is three quarters of a wave, but both are measured from the antinode, which sits slightly beyond the open rim by the end correction.
So the two conditions carry an unknown e in each. That looks awkward, but it is the key to a clean escape.
Write them down. The first column plus the end correction equals a quarter wavelength; the second column plus the end correction equals three quarters of a wavelength.
There they are, both sharing the same unknown end correction.

Now the master move. Subtract the two equations and the end correction cancels completely. The difference of the columns is half a wavelength, so the wavelength is twice fifty two minus seventeen, that is seventy centimetres, and the speed of sound is frequency times wavelength, four hundred eighty times zero point seven metres, three hundred thirty six metres per second.

With the wavelength known, back out the end correction. A quarter of seventy is seventeen point five centimetres, and the first column was seventeen, so the end correction is zero point five centimetres.
<whisper>The lesson to keep: subtracting the two resonance conditions kills the end correction and hands you the wavelength cleanly. Then you recover e afterward.</whisper>

J E E Advanced version, जहाँ end correction आख़िरकार मायने रखता है। four hundred eighty hertz का tuning fork एक resonance tube को drive करता है। पहली resonance तब आती है जब air column seventeen centimetre हो, दूसरी fifty two centimetre पर। Speed of sound और end correction निकालो।

Insight figure में है। Resonance tube एक closed pipe है, क्योंकि water surface sealed closed end की तरह काम करता है। पहली resonance a quarter wave है, दूसरी three quarters of a wave, पर दोनों antinode से नापी जाती हैं, जो open rim से ज़रा आगे end correction जितना ऊपर बैठता है।
तो दोनों conditions में एक unknown e है। ये अजीब लगता है, पर यही एक साफ़ escape की चाबी है।
इन्हें लिखो। पहला column plus end correction equals a quarter wavelength; दूसरा column plus end correction equals three quarters of a wavelength।
ये रहीं, दोनों एक ही unknown end correction share करती हुईं।

<excited>अब master move। दोनों equations को subtract करो और end correction पूरी तरह cancel हो जाता है। Columns का difference half a wavelength है, तो wavelength है twice of fifty two minus seventeen, यानी seventy centimetre, और speed of sound है frequency into wavelength, four hundred eighty into zero point seven metre, three hundred thirty six metre per second।</excited>
Wavelength पता चलने पर end correction निकालो। Seventy का a quarter है seventeen point five centimetre, और पहला column seventeen था, तो end correction है zero point five centimetre।
याद रखने वाला सबक़ — दोनों resonance conditions को subtract करना end correction को मार देता है और wavelength साफ़ दे देता है। फिर e को बाद में recover करो।

sections.title: Common pitfalls and pro-tips

board_events.text: Common pitfalls and pro-tips
Pitfall 1: mislabelling overtones in closed pipes - the first overtone is the 3rd harmonic, not the 2nd.
Pitfall 2: forgetting the end correction - the antinode lies about 0.6 r beyond the open end.
But subtracting two resonance lengths cancels the end correction, so lean on that.
Pitfall 3: confusing node/antinode spacing - node to node is half a wavelength, node to antinode a quarter.
Pitfall 4: mixing displacement and pressure - a closed end is a displacement node but a pressure antinode.
Pro-tip: for three successive resonances, take the common gap. Smallest over gap a whole number means open; else closed.
Open: fundamental = gap. Closed: fundamental = gap over 2. Identifies the pipe in seconds.

segments.text: The four traps that quietly wreck acoustics answers, then one shortcut that identifies any pipe in five seconds.
Trap one. In a closed pipe, the first overtone is the third harmonic, not the second. Overtone counts the allowed frequencies above the fundamental, and for a closed pipe those skip the evens.

Trap two. In precise resonance tube work, the antinode does not sit exactly at the open end; it lies about zero point six times the radius beyond it. Ignoring the end correction gives a slightly wrong speed of sound.
But there is a clean dodge. Subtracting two resonance lengths cancels the end correction entirely, so whenever you can, subtract.
Trap three. Do not muddle the spacings. Node to node is half a wavelength; node to nearest antinode is a quarter. Sketch one loop and label it, and half these errors vanish.

Trap four, the subtle one. Displacement and pressure patterns are always opposite. At a closed end you have a displacement node but a pressure antinode. Questions that ask for the pressure antinode trip students who only think in displacement.

Now the pro-tip that pays every time. For three successive resonance frequencies, take the common gap. If the smallest frequency divided by that gap is a whole number, it is an open pipe and the fundamental equals the gap.
If it is not a whole number, it is a closed pipe and the fundamental is the gap divided by two. That one check names the pipe and its fundamental in about five seconds, no diagrams needed.
<excited>चार traps जो चुपचाप acoustics के answers बिगाड़ते हैं, फिर एक shortcut जो किसी भी pipe को five seconds में पहचान लेता है।</excited>
Trap one। Closed pipe में first overtone third harmonic है, second नहीं। Overtone fundamental के ऊपर allowed frequencies गिनता है, और closed pipe के लिए वो evens skip करते हैं।
Trap two। Precise resonance tube work में antinode बिल्कुल open end पर नहीं बैठता; वो उससे लगभग zero point six into radius आगे होता है। End correction ignore करना speed of sound ज़रा ग़लत देता है।
पर एक साफ़ dodge है। दो resonance lengths को subtract करना end correction पूरी तरह cancel कर देता है, तो जब भी हो सके, subtract करो।
Trap three। Spacings मत गड्डमड्ड करो। Node to node half a wavelength; node to nearest antinode a quarter। एक loop बनाकर label करो, और इनमें से आधी गलतियाँ ग़ायब।

Trap four, subtle वाला। Displacement और pressure patterns हमेशा opposite होते हैं। Closed end पर displacement node होता है पर pressure antinode। जो questions pressure antinode पूछते हैं वो सिर्फ़ displacement में सोचने वालों को गिरा देते हैं।

अब वो pro-tip जो हर बार काम आती है। तीन successive resonance frequencies के लिए common gap लो। अगर सबसे छोटी frequency उस gap से divide करने पर whole number हो, तो open pipe और fundamental gap के बराबर।
अगर whole number न हो, तो closed pipe और fundamental gap divided by two। वो एक check pipe और उसका fundamental लगभग five seconds में बता देता है, बिना diagrams।

board_events.text: A train's horn sounds high as it approaches, then drops as it passes. The horn never changed - the observed frequency did.
This change in observed frequency from relative motion between source and observer is the Doppler effect.
Toward = frequency up. Away = frequency down. Every Doppler answer must pass this gut check.
Source rushing toward you: each new wavefront is launched closer, so they bunch - shorter wavelength, higher pitch.
Source racing away: wavefronts are launched farther back - longer wavelength, lower pitch.
Move yourself instead: walk into the waves and meet more per second (higher); walk away and meet fewer (lower).

segments.text: <curious>You are standing at a railway crossing. A train rushes toward you, horn blaring at a high, urgent pitch. The instant it passes and speeds away, the pitch suddenly drops. The driver inside hears no change at all. So what happened?
The figure holds the mechanism. As the source moves, the wavefronts it emits bunch up ahead of it and spread out behind. Bunched means shorter wavelength; spread means longer.
That apparent change in the observed frequency, caused purely by the relative motion between source and observer, is the Doppler effect. Notice the horn itself never changed its note.
Let me state it cleanly. The Doppler effect is the change in the frequency you observe when the source and the observer move relative to each other.

And here is the one gut check that governs everything. Toward means frequency up; away means frequency down. If your formula ever gives a higher frequency while source and observer are separating, you have made a sign error, full stop.

Now the why, for a moving source. If the source is rushing toward you, each new wavefront is launched a little closer to you than the last, so the wavefronts crowd together. A shorter wavelength reaching your ear is heard as a higher pitch.
When the source races away, each wavefront is launched farther back, the waves stretch out, the wavelength grows, and you hear a lower pitch.
The same logic works if you move instead. Walk toward a stationary source and you sweep through more wavefronts per second, higher frequency. Walk away and you meet fewer per second, lower frequency.

<curious>तुम railway crossing पर खड़े हो। एक train तुम्हारी तरफ़ दौड़ती है, horn ऊँची, urgent pitch पर बज रहा। जैसे ही वो गुज़रकर दूर भागती है, pitch अचानक गिर जाती है। अंदर बैठा driver कोई change नहीं सुनता। तो हुआ क्या?
Figure mechanism पकड़ लेता है। जैसे source move करता है, उसके छोड़े wavefronts उसके आगे bunch हो जाते हैं और पीछे फैल जाते हैं। Bunched यानी छोटी wavelength; spread यानी लंबी।
Observed frequency में वो apparent change, सिर्फ़ source और observer के बीच relative motion से, Doppler effect है। ध्यान दो horn ने खुद अपना note कभी बदला ही नहीं।
इसे साफ़ कहूँ। Doppler effect वो change है observed frequency में जब source और observer एक-दूसरे के relative move करते हैं।

<excited>और यहाँ वो एक gut check है जो सब कुछ चलाता है। Toward यानी frequency up; away यानी frequency down। अगर तुम्हारा formula कभी source और observer के अलग होते हुए higher frequency दे, तो तुमने sign error किया है, बस।</excited>

अब why, moving source के लिए। अगर source तुम्हारी तरफ़ दौड़ रहा है, हर नया wavefront पिछले से थोड़ा और पास launch होता है, तो wavefronts भीड़ बना लेते हैं। तुम्हारे कान तक पहुँचती छोटी wavelength higher pitch सुनाई देती है।
जब source दूर भागता है, हर wavefront और पीछे launch होता है, waves खिंच जाती हैं, wavelength बढ़ती है, और तुम lower pitch सुनते हो।
वही logic तब भी चलता है जब तुम move करो। किसी stationary source की तरफ़ चलो और तुम per second ज़्यादा wavefronts sweep करते हो, higher frequency। दूर चलो और per second कम मिलते हैं, lower frequency।

board_events.text: For sound, moving the source is NOT the same as moving the observer.
A moving source physically compresses the wavelength in the medium. A moving observer meets unchanged waves at a changed effective speed.
Two mechanisms, two formulas, two slightly different answers - even at the same speed.
Sound needs a medium, a fixed stage all motion is measured against. Light, having no medium, is symmetric.
Doppler is everywhere: radar speed guns, submarine sonar, and the redshift of galaxies that revealed an expanding universe.
Limits: only the along-the-line velocity counts; wind shifts the sound speed; the source must stay below the sound speed.

segments.text: Now the subtlety that J E E and N E E T examiners adore, because it separates the students who truly understand Doppler from those who only memorised a formula.
The figure puts the two cases side by side. On the left the source moves; on the right the observer moves. They are not the same, and the picture shows why.
The key claim is this. For sound, moving the source is not the same as moving the observer, even at identical speeds.

Here is the difference. When the source moves, it physically crowds or stretches the wavelength in the air itself. When the observer moves, the wavelength in the air is unchanged; instead the observer changes the effective speed at which they meet the waves.
Two different mechanisms give two different formulas and two slightly different answers, even for the same speed. That is the asymmetry, and it is a favourite trap.

Why does sound behave this way? Because sound needs a medium, and that medium, the air, is a fixed stage against which every motion is measured. Light has no medium, so for light only the relative velocity matters and the effect is perfectly symmetric.

<whisper>And Doppler is genuinely everywhere.</whisper> The highway radar gun bounces microwaves off your car and reads the frequency shift to catch speeding. A submarine sonar tracks another vessel by the shift. And astronomers measure the redshift of distant galaxies, light stretched to longer, redder wavelengths, which told us the universe is expanding.

Three limits to respect. Only the velocity component along the line joining source and observer counts, so at closest approach there is no shift for sound. Wind changes the effective sound speed and must be added in. And the source speed must stay below the speed of sound, or the wavefronts pile into a shock wave and the ordinary formula breaks.
अब वो subtlety जो J E E और N E E T examiners को बहुत पसंद है, क्योंकि ये उन students को अलग करती है जो सच में Doppler समझते हैं और जिन्होंने बस formula रट लिया।
Figure दोनों cases को साथ रखता है। बाईं तरफ़ source move करता है; दाईं तरफ़ observer। ये same नहीं हैं, और picture दिखाता है क्यों।
Key claim ये है। Sound के लिए source move करना observer move करने जैसा नहीं है, भले speeds बराबर हों।

फ़र्क़ ये है। जब source move करता है, वो air में ही wavelength को crowd या stretch कर देता है। जब observer move करता है, air में wavelength unchanged रहती है; बल्कि observer वो effective speed बदल देता है जिस पर वो waves से मिलता है।
दो अलग mechanisms दो अलग formulas और दो ज़रा अलग answers देते हैं, same speed पर भी। यही asymmetry है, और यही favourite trap है।

Sound ऐसा क्यों करता है? क्योंकि sound को medium चाहिए, और वो medium, यानी air, एक fixed stage है जिसके against हर motion नापी जाती है। Light का कोई medium नहीं, तो light के लिए सिर्फ़ relative velocity मायने रखती है और effect perfectly symmetric है।

<excited>और Doppler सच में हर जगह है। Highway radar gun तुम्हारी car से microwaves टकराकर frequency shift पढ़ता है speeding पकड़ने के लिए। Submarine sonar दूसरे vessel को shift से track करता है। और astronomers दूर galaxies की redshift नापते हैं, light लंबी, लाल wavelengths तक खिंची, जिसने बताया कि universe फैल रहा है।</excited>

तीन limits का ख़याल रखो। सिर्फ़ source और observer को जोड़ती line के साथ वाला velocity component गिनता है, तो closest approach पर sound के लिए कोई shift नहीं। Wind effective sound speed बदलता है और जोड़ना पड़ता है। और source speed sound speed से नीचे रहनी चाहिए, वरना wavefronts एक shock wave में ढेर हो जाते हैं और साधारण formula टूट जाता है।

segments.text: Let us derive both basic Doppler cases and, most importantly, see exactly why they differ.
Case A first: the source moves toward a stationary observer. Let the source emit frequency f, so its period is one over f, and let sound travel at speed v.

Here is the key event, shown in the figure. During one period, the source itself advances a distance v s times T toward the observer. So by the time it emits the next crest, it has crept forward, and the gap between consecutive crests, the wavelength reaching the observer, is squeezed.

That squeezed wavelength is v T minus v s T, which is v minus v s over f. The sound still travels at speed v, set by the medium, so the observed frequency is v over that new wavelength, giving f times v over v minus v s. Since the denominator is smaller than v, the frequency rises, exactly as approach demands.
Case B: now the observer moves toward a stationary source. This time the source is still, so the wavelength in the air is the normal v over f, unchanged.

But the observer is rushing into the waves at speed v o, so relative to them the sound arrives at an effective speed v plus v o. The number of wavefronts they sweep per second is that effective speed over the wavelength, which gives f times v plus v o over v. Again the frequency rises.

Now compare them at the same speed u. Source moving gives f times v over v minus u; observer moving gives f times v plus u over v. These are not equal, and the source-moving result is slightly larger. A moving source changes the wavelength; a moving observer changes the effective speed.
Combining both motions gives the general formula: f prime equals f times v plus v o over v minus v s. Learn the sign logic, not four separate formulas.
दोनों basic Doppler cases derive करते हैं और, सबसे ज़रूरी, ठीक-ठीक देखते हैं कि वो अलग क्यों हैं।
पहले Case A — source stationary observer की तरफ़ move करता है। मान लो source frequency f emit करता है, तो उसका period one over f है, और sound speed v से चलती है।

यहाँ key event है, figure में दिखा। एक period के दौरान source खुद observer की तरफ़ v s into T दूरी आगे बढ़ता है। तो जब तक वो अगला crest emit करता है, वो आगे खिसक चुका होता है, और consecutive crests के बीच का gap, यानी observer तक पहुँचती wavelength, squeeze हो जाती है।

वो squeezed wavelength है v T minus v s T, यानी v minus v s over f। Sound अब भी speed v से चलती है, medium से तय, तो observed frequency है v over उस नई wavelength, यानी f into v over v minus v s। Denominator v से छोटा है, तो frequency बढ़ती है, बिल्कुल जैसा approach चाहता है।
Case B — अब observer stationary source की तरफ़ move करता है। इस बार source स्थिर है, तो air में wavelength normal v over f है, unchanged।

पर observer speed v o से waves में घुस रहा है, तो उसके relative sound effective speed v plus v o से आती है। वो per second जितने wavefronts sweep करता है वो है effective speed over wavelength, यानी f into v plus v o over v। फिर frequency बढ़ती है।

<whisper>अब उन्हें same speed u पर compare करो। Source moving देता है f into v over v minus u; observer moving देता है f into v plus u over v। ये बराबर नहीं हैं, और source-moving वाला result ज़रा बड़ा है। Moving source wavelength बदलता है; moving observer effective speed।</whisper>
दोनों motions मिलाकर general formula मिलता है — f prime equals f into v plus v o over v minus v s। Sign logic सीखो, चार अलग formulas नहीं।

board_events.text: Doppler effect - the toolkit
Sign rule: +v_o in the numerator if the observer moves toward; -v_s in the denominator if the source moves toward.

segments.text: The full Doppler toolkit. Anchor all of it to the single idea that motion toward raises pitch.
The master formula for sound: f prime equals f times v plus or minus v o, over v minus or plus v s. The signs are chosen by the physics, never memorised blindly.

The sign rule. Use plus v o in the numerator if the observer moves toward the source, and minus v s in the denominator if the source moves toward the observer. Both choices are just toward raises pitch.
The two clean special cases: source moving toward a still observer gives f times v over v minus v s; observer moving toward a still source gives f times v plus v o over v.
When both approach, the numerator gains v o and the denominator loses v s, giving f times v plus v o over v minus v s. The highest shift of the lot.
For wind of speed w blowing from source to observer, simply replace v with v plus w everywhere. If the wind blows the other way, use v minus w. It applies to both the numerator and the denominator.
For light, when the relative speed is much less than the speed of light, the observed frequency is f times one plus or minus u over c, and the fractional wavelength shift equals u over c.
Finally the colour code. Approaching gives a blueshift, frequency up, wavelength down. Receding gives a redshift, frequency down, wavelength up. Red runs away.
पूरा Doppler toolkit। इस सब को एक ही idea पर anchor करो कि toward वाली motion pitch बढ़ाती है।
Sound का master formula — f prime equals f into v plus या minus v o, over v minus या plus v s। Signs physics से चुने जाते हैं, कभी आँख मूँदकर रटे नहीं।
Sign rule। Numerator में plus v o अगर observer source की तरफ़ move करे, और denominator में minus v s अगर source observer की तरफ़ move करे। दोनों choices बस toward raises pitch हैं।
दो साफ़ special cases — source still observer की तरफ़ देता है f into v over v minus v s; observer still source की तरफ़ देता है f into v plus v o over v।
जब दोनों approach करें, numerator को v o मिलता है और denominator से v s घटता है, यानी f into v plus v o over v minus v s। सबसे बड़ा shift।
Source से observer की तरफ़ बहती w speed की wind के लिए, बस v को v plus w से replace करो हर जगह। Wind उल्टी बहे तो v minus w। ये numerator और denominator दोनों पर लगता है।
Light के लिए, जब relative speed speed of light से बहुत कम हो, observed frequency है f into one plus या minus u over c, और fractional wavelength shift बराबर u over c।
आख़िर में colour code। Approaching देता है blueshift, frequency up, wavelength down। Receding देता है redshift, frequency down, wavelength up। Red runs away।

segments.text: A clean board-level Doppler numerical. A train approaches a stationary listener on a platform at thirty metres per second, sounding a horn of five hundred hertz. With the speed of sound three hundred thirty metres per second, find the frequency the listener hears.
The figure sets the scene: an approaching source and a still listener. Approach means the pitch must rise, so we already know the answer exceeds five hundred.
Reading the data: true frequency five hundred, source speed thirty toward the observer, observer speed zero, sound speed three hundred thirty.
This is a source moving toward a stationary observer, so the observer term drops out and we use minus v s in the denominator, which makes the fraction bigger.
Plug in. f prime is five hundred times three hundred thirty over three hundred thirty minus thirty.
That is five hundred times three hundred thirty over three hundred, which is five hundred times one point one, giving five hundred fifty hertz.
Sanity check. Five hundred fifty is higher than the true five hundred, exactly what an approaching source should produce.
So the listener hears five hundred fifty hertz.

एक साफ़ board-level Doppler numerical। एक train platform पर खड़े stationary listener की तरफ़ thirty metre per second से आती है, five hundred hertz का horn बजाते हुए। Speed of sound three hundred thirty metre per second, listener को सुनाई देने वाली frequency निकालो।
Figure scene set करता है — approaching source और स्थिर listener। Approach यानी pitch बढ़ेगी, तो हमें पहले से पता है answer five hundred से ज़्यादा है।
Data पढ़ो — true frequency five hundred, source speed thirty observer की तरफ़, observer speed zero, sound speed three hundred thirty।
ये source stationary observer की तरफ़ move कर रहा है, तो observer term हट जाता है और हम denominator में minus v s use करते हैं, जो fraction बड़ा कर देता है।
Plug in करो। f prime है five hundred into three hundred thirty over three hundred thirty minus thirty।
यानी five hundred into three hundred thirty over three hundred, जो five hundred into one point one, यानी five hundred fifty hertz।
Sanity check। Five hundred fifty true five hundred से ज़्यादा है, बिल्कुल जैसा approaching source देना चाहिए।
तो listener five hundred fifty hertz सुनता है।

board_events.text: True frequency 300 Hz, sound speed 330 m/s. Case 1: source at 30 toward. Case 2: observer at 30 toward. Equal?
The trap: same speed, same approach, so surely the same frequency. Wrong - sound is asymmetric.
The two differ because a moving source compresses the wavelength, while a moving observer only changes the meeting rate.
Answer: not equal. Source-moving beats observer-moving for approach.

segments.text: This N E E T question is built entirely on the asymmetry we just derived. The true frequency is three hundred hertz and the speed of sound is three hundred thirty. In case one the source moves toward a still observer at thirty metres per second; in case two the observer moves toward a still source at the same thirty. Are the two observed frequencies equal?
The figure warns you: same speed on both sides, but the mechanisms differ.
So the whole question is whether swapping who moves changes the answer.
Here is the trap. Same speed, same approach, so students confidently say the frequencies must be equal. They are not, because sound Doppler is asymmetric.

Case one, source moving. f prime is three hundred times three hundred thirty over three hundred thirty minus thirty, which is three hundred times three hundred thirty over three hundred, giving three hundred thirty hertz.

Case two, observer moving. f prime is three hundred times three hundred thirty plus thirty over three hundred thirty, which is three hundred times three hundred sixty over three hundred thirty, giving three hundred twenty seven point three hertz.
They differ because a moving source physically compresses the wavelength in the air, while a moving observer leaves the wavelength alone and merely changes the rate of meeting waves.

So the answer is no, they are not equal. For approach the source-moving shift always beats the observer-moving shift, and the two only nearly coincide when both speeds are far below the speed of sound.

ये N E E T question पूरी तरह उसी asymmetry पर बना है जो हमने अभी derive की। True frequency three hundred hertz है और speed of sound three hundred thirty। Case one में source स्थिर observer की तरफ़ thirty metre per second से; case two में observer स्थिर source की तरफ़ उसी thirty से। क्या दोनों observed frequencies बराबर हैं?
Figure warn करता है — दोनों तरफ़ same speed, पर mechanisms अलग।
तो पूरा सवाल ये है कि कौन move कर रहा है, ये बदलने से answer बदलता है क्या।
यहाँ trap है। Same speed, same approach, तो students confidently कहते हैं frequencies बराबर होंगी। नहीं हैं, क्योंकि sound Doppler asymmetric है।

<excited>Case one, source moving। f prime है three hundred into three hundred thirty over three hundred thirty minus thirty, यानी three hundred into three hundred thirty over three hundred, जो three hundred thirty hertz।</excited>

Case two, observer moving। f prime है three hundred into three hundred thirty plus thirty over three hundred thirty, यानी three hundred into three hundred sixty over three hundred thirty, जो three hundred twenty seven point three hertz।
ये अलग हैं क्योंकि moving source air में wavelength को physically compress करता है, जबकि moving observer wavelength को छोड़ देता है और बस waves से मिलने की rate बदलता है।
तो answer है नहीं, ये बराबर नहीं हैं। Approach के लिए source-moving shift हमेशा observer-moving shift से बड़ा होता है, और दोनों तभी लगभग बराबर होते हैं जब दोनों speeds sound speed से बहुत नीचे हों।

segments.text: A staple J E E Main Doppler numerical with both parties moving. An ambulance with a siren of six hundred hertz moves toward a motorcyclist at forty metres per second, while the motorcyclist rides toward the ambulance at twenty metres per second. The speed of sound is three hundred forty. Find the frequency the rider hears.
The figure shows them closing on each other, so before any algebra we know the pitch must climb.
Collect the data: true frequency six hundred, source speed forty toward, observer speed twenty toward, sound speed three hundred forty.
Both are approaching, so the numerator gains plus v o and the denominator gains minus v s. Both changes push the frequency up.
Plug in. f prime is six hundred times three hundred forty plus twenty over three hundred forty minus forty.
That is six hundred times three hundred sixty over three hundred, which is six hundred times one point two, giving seven hundred twenty hertz.
Sanity check. Both parties race toward each other, so the frequency must rise well above six hundred, and seven hundred twenty comfortably does.
So the rider hears seven hundred twenty hertz.

एक staple J E E Main Doppler numerical, दोनों parties moving। एक ambulance six hundred hertz की siren के साथ motorcyclist की तरफ़ forty metre per second से आती है, जबकि motorcyclist ambulance की तरफ़ twenty metre per second से आता है। Speed of sound three hundred forty। Rider को सुनाई देने वाली frequency निकालो।
Figure उन्हें एक-दूसरे की तरफ़ बढ़ते दिखाता है, तो किसी algebra से पहले ही पता है pitch चढ़ेगी।
Data इकट्ठा करो — true frequency six hundred, source speed forty toward, observer speed twenty toward, sound speed three hundred forty।
दोनों approach कर रहे हैं, तो numerator को plus v o मिलता है और denominator को minus v s। दोनों changes frequency ऊपर धकेलते हैं।
Plug in करो। f prime है six hundred into three hundred forty plus twenty over three hundred forty minus forty।
यानी six hundred into three hundred sixty over three hundred, जो six hundred into one point two, यानी seven hundred twenty hertz।
Sanity check। दोनों एक-दूसरे की तरफ़ दौड़ते हैं, तो frequency six hundred से काफ़ी ऊपर उठनी चाहिए, और seven hundred twenty आराम से करती है।
तो rider seven hundred twenty hertz सुनता है।

segments.text: The J E E Advanced showpiece, a double Doppler. A car moving toward a large vertical wall at twenty metres per second sounds a horn of three hundred twenty hertz. The speed of sound is three hundred forty. Find the frequency of the echo the driver hears, and the beat frequency between the direct horn and the echo.

The figure reveals the trick. The wall first acts as a moving-source to stationary-observer problem, then re-emits as a stationary-source to moving-observer problem. The driver is both the original source and the final listener.
So we do it in two Doppler steps and then read off the beats.
Step one, sound reaches the wall. The wall is a stationary observer, and the car is a source approaching at twenty.
So the wall receives f times v over v minus u, that is three hundred twenty times three hundred forty over three hundred twenty, which is three hundred forty hertz.
Step two, the wall reflects. It now behaves as a stationary source emitting three hundred forty hertz, and the driver is an observer moving toward it at twenty.

So the echo is three hundred forty times three hundred sixty over three hundred forty, which is three hundred sixty hertz. The combined shortcut, f times v plus u over v minus u, lands on the same three hundred sixty.

<excited>Finally the beats. The driver also hears the horn directly at its true three hundred twenty. The beat between the echo and the direct sound is three hundred sixty minus three hundred twenty, which is forty hertz, and it grows as the car speeds up.</excited>

J E E Advanced का showpiece, एक double Doppler। एक car बड़ी vertical wall की तरफ़ twenty metre per second से three hundred twenty hertz का horn बजाती है। Speed of sound three hundred forty। Driver को सुनाई देने वाले echo की frequency, और direct horn और echo के बीच beat frequency निकालो।

<whisper>Figure trick खोल देता है। Wall पहले moving-source to stationary-observer problem की तरह काम करती है, फिर stationary-source to moving-observer की तरह re-emit करती है। Driver दोनों है — original source और final listener।</whisper>
तो हम इसे दो Doppler steps में करते हैं और फिर beats पढ़ते हैं।
Step one, sound wall तक पहुँचती है। Wall stationary observer है, और car twenty से approach करता source।
तो wall को मिलता है f into v over v minus u, यानी three hundred twenty into three hundred forty over three hundred twenty, जो three hundred forty hertz।
Step two, wall reflect करती है। अब ये three hundred forty hertz emit करता stationary source है, और driver उसकी तरफ़ twenty से move करता observer।

तो echo है three hundred forty into three hundred sixty over three hundred forty, यानी three hundred sixty hertz। Combined shortcut, f into v plus u over v minus u, भी उसी three hundred sixty पर आता है।

आख़िर में beats। Driver horn को सीधे उसकी true three hundred twenty पर भी सुनता है। Echo और direct sound के बीच beat है three hundred sixty minus three hundred twenty, यानी forty hertz, और car तेज़ होने पर ये बढ़ता है।

sections.title: Common pitfalls and pro-tips

board_events.text: Common pitfalls and pro-tips
Pitfall 1: sign-convention chaos. Do not memorise four formulas - anchor to toward up, away down, and fix signs to match.
Pitfall 2: treating source-moving and observer-moving as identical. Use v_s in the denominator, v_o in the numerator.
Pitfall 3: ignoring the wind. It shifts the sound speed: v becomes v plus or minus w in both numerator and denominator.
Pitfall 4: using the off-axis velocity. Only the component along the line of sight counts.
At the moment of closest approach the motion is pure sideways, so there is no Doppler shift for sound.
Pro-tip: for a car hearing its own echo off a wall, use the combined result directly.
Echo: f' = f (v + u)/(v - u); beat with the direct sound: f_beat = 2 u f / (v - u).

segments.text: The four Doppler traps, then the one-line shortcut for wall echoes.

Trap one, and the single most common error: sign-convention chaos. Do not blindly memorise four formulas. Anchor every problem to toward raises pitch, away lowers it, and assign the signs so the result matches. If it does not, flip a sign.
Trap two. Do not treat source-moving and observer-moving as identical; they give different answers for sound. Keep v s in the denominator and v o in the numerator, and never swap them.

Trap three. Do not ignore the wind. Wind changes the effective sound speed, so v becomes v plus or minus w in both the numerator and the denominator. Students often forget it applies everywhere, or get its direction backward.
Trap four. Do not plug in the full off-axis velocity. Only the component along the line joining source and observer counts.
In particular, at the exact moment of closest approach the motion is purely sideways, so there is no Doppler shift at all for sound. That single fact answers many tricky questions.
Now the pro-tip. For a source approaching a wall and hearing its own echo, skip the two-step grind and use the combined result directly.

The echo frequency is f times v plus u over v minus u, and the beat with the direct sound is two u f over v minus u. Recognising the wall as a stationary mirror turns a messy double Doppler into one clean line.
चार Doppler traps, फिर wall echoes के लिए एक-line shortcut।

Trap one, और सबसे common error — sign-convention chaos। चार formulas आँख मूँदकर मत रटो। हर problem को toward raises pitch, away lowers it पर anchor करो, और signs ऐसे assign करो कि result match करे। न करे तो एक sign flip कर दो।
Trap two। Source-moving और observer-moving को identical मत समझो; ये sound के लिए अलग answers देते हैं। v s को denominator में और v o को numerator में रखो, और कभी swap मत करो।

Trap three। Wind को ignore मत करो। Wind effective sound speed बदलता है, तो v बनता है v plus या minus w, numerator और denominator दोनों में। Students अक्सर भूल जाते हैं कि ये हर जगह लगता है, या direction उल्टी कर देते हैं।
Trap four। पूरी off-axis velocity plug मत करो। सिर्फ़ source और observer को जोड़ती line के साथ वाला component गिनता है।
<excited>ख़ासकर, closest approach के ठीक पल पर motion बिल्कुल sideways होती है, तो sound के लिए कोई Doppler shift नहीं। वो एक fact कई मुश्किल सवालों का जवाब है।</excited>
अब pro-tip। किसी source के wall की तरफ़ बढ़ते हुए अपना echo सुनने के लिए, two-step grind छोड़ो और combined result सीधे use करो।
Echo frequency है f into v plus u over v minus u, और direct sound के साथ beat है two u f over v minus u। Wall को stationary mirror समझना एक messy double Doppler को एक साफ़ line में बदल देता है।

sections.title: Formula recap: the complete Waves toolkit

board_events.text: Formula recap: your complete Waves toolkit

board_events.latex: f' = f\!\left(\dfrac{v \pm v_o}{v \mp v_s}\right); \quad \text{echo beat: } f_{\text{beat}} = \dfrac{2uf}{v - u}

board_events.text: This is your complete toolkit - every chapter formula in one frame. Recall it, do not re-derive it.

segments.text: Before the cheat sheet, here is your complete toolkit for the whole Waves chapter, every formula in one frame. This is for recall, not re-teaching, so I will name each one, not derive it.

From wave basics: speed equals frequency times wavelength, equals wavelength over period, equals omega over k; the string speed is root T over mu; and the maximum particle speed is amplitude times omega.

From superposition: the resultant amplitude is the root of A one squared plus A two squared plus twice A one A two cosine phi, and the maximum and minimum intensities are the square of root I one plus or minus root I two.
From beats: the beat frequency is the absolute difference of the two frequencies, and since frequency goes as root T, the fractional frequency change is half the fractional tension change.
From standing waves: a string or open pipe has frequencies n v over two L with all harmonics, while a closed pipe has two n minus one, times v over four L, with only the odd harmonics.
From the resonance tube: the wavelength is twice the difference of the two resonance lengths, and the end correction is l two minus three l one, over two.
And from Doppler: f prime is f times v plus or minus v o, over v minus or plus v s; and for a car hearing its wall echo, the beat is two u f over v minus u.
That is the entire chapter on one board. If you can look at each line and immediately say what it does, you are ready. Recall it; do not re-derive it under exam pressure.
Cheat sheet से पहले, ये रहा पूरे Waves chapter का complete toolkit, हर formula एक frame में। ये recall के लिए है, दोबारा पढ़ाने के लिए नहीं, तो मैं हर एक का नाम लूँगा, derive नहीं करूँगा।
Wave basics से — speed equals frequency into wavelength, equals wavelength over period, equals omega over k; string speed है root T over mu; और maximum particle speed है amplitude into omega।

Superposition से — resultant amplitude है root of A one squared plus A two squared plus twice A one A two cosine phi, और maximum और minimum intensities हैं root I one plus या minus root I two का square।
Beats से — beat frequency दोनों frequencies का absolute difference है, और frequency root T की तरह चलती है, तो fractional frequency change fractional tension change का आधा है।
Standing waves से — string या open pipe की frequencies हैं n v over two L सारे harmonics के साथ, जबकि closed pipe की हैं two n minus one, into v over four L, सिर्फ़ odd harmonics के साथ।
Resonance tube से — wavelength दोनों resonance lengths के difference का दोगुना है, और end correction है l two minus three l one, over two।
और Doppler से — f prime है f into v plus या minus v o, over v minus या plus v s; और car के wall echo के लिए beat है two u f over v minus u।
यही पूरा chapter एक board पर है। अगर तुम हर line देखकर तुरंत बता सको कि वो क्या करती है, तो तुम ready हो। इसे recall करो; exam pressure में दोबारा derive मत करो।

sections.title: Cheat sheet: Waves quick recall

board_events.text: Cheat sheet: Waves quick recall
Tight and light goes fast: high tension, low mass density means high speed - never A or f.
Source sets the frequency; the medium sets the speed.
Beats: the plain difference, no halving. Same f gives a pattern in space; close f gives a throb in time.
Wax weighs it down (lowers f); filing files it up (raises f).
Closed = odd only; open = all. Closed pipe's first overtone leapfrogs to 3 f1.
Subtract the resonance lengths and the end correction disappears.
Toward raises, away lowers. v_s below, v_o on top. Red runs away (redshift = receding).

segments.text: <excited>And finally, the cheat sheet, the memory aids you carry into the exam hall. These are the one-liners that recover a whole method in a heartbeat.</excited>
For wave speed on a string: tight and light goes fast. High tension and low mass density mean a high speed, and neither amplitude nor frequency ever touches it.
For the master relation: the source sets the frequency, and the medium sets the speed. Cross into a new medium and frequency stays fixed while speed and wavelength adjust together.
For beats: it is the plain difference, no halving. And keep the two scenarios apart, same frequency gives a pattern in space, close frequencies give a throb in time.
For tuning forks: wax weighs it down, so loading lowers the frequency, and filing files it up, raising it. That fixes your plus or minus every time.
For pipes: closed means odd harmonics only, open means all of them. And remember the closed pipe's first overtone leapfrogs straight to three f one.
For the resonance tube: subtract the two resonance lengths and the end correction disappears, handing you a clean wavelength.

And for Doppler: toward raises, away lowers; v s sits below in the denominator, v o on top in the numerator; and red runs away, since a redshift means the source is receding. Carry these eight lines and the whole chapter comes back on demand.
और आख़िर में, cheat sheet, वो memory aids जो तुम exam hall में ले जाते हो। ये वो one-liners हैं जो एक पल में पूरा method वापस ला देते हैं।
String पर wave speed के लिए — tight and light goes fast। High tension और low mass density यानी high speed, और amplitude या frequency इसे कभी नहीं छूते।
Master relation के लिए — source frequency तय करता है, और medium speed। नए medium में जाओ तो frequency fixed रहती है जबकि speed और wavelength साथ adjust होते हैं।
Beats के लिए — plain difference, कोई halving नहीं। और दोनों scenarios अलग रखो — same frequency space में pattern देती है, close frequencies time में throb।
Tuning forks के लिए — wax weighs it down, तो loading frequency गिराता है, और filing files it up, बढ़ाता है। वो हर बार तुम्हारा plus या minus ठीक कर देता है।
Pipes के लिए — closed यानी सिर्फ़ odd harmonics, open यानी सारे। और याद रखो closed pipe का first overtone सीधे three f one पर leapfrog करता है।
Resonance tube के लिए — दोनों resonance lengths को subtract करो और end correction ग़ायब हो जाता है, एक साफ़ wavelength देकर।

<excited>और Doppler के लिए — toward raises, away lowers; v s नीचे denominator में बैठता है, v o ऊपर numerator में; और red runs away, क्योंकि redshift यानी source receding। ये आठ lines रखो और पूरा chapter demand पर वापस आ जाता है।</excited>
